operator.payload: Should the new repeatable flags be named `--field <name>` and `--field-id <id>`, matching `gh project item-edit`?
operator.answer: OPERATOR_ANSWER: Yes. Use repeatable `--field <name>` and `--field-id <id>` flags; they are mutually exclusive.

operator.payload: Add repeatable, mutually exclusive `--field <name>` and `--field-id <id>` flags to `gh project item-list`. Resolve every supplied selector against the project fields returned by the existing item-list GraphQL response, so no separate field preflight request is made. `--field` matches names case-insensitively; an unknown name reports the supplied name plus sorted available field names, an ambiguous name reports matching IDs and directs the user to `--field-id`, and an unknown ID reports sorted `name (id)` candidates. Preserve selector order for the added columns; headers use each resolved field’s canonical project field name and columns are appended after the existing Type, Title, Number, Repository, and ID columns. An item with no value for a selected field renders an empty cell. Render human-readable values by field-value type: date/text/single-select as their text; number as a normal decimal; iteration and milestone as title; labels, users, reviewers, and pull requests as comma-separated names or URLs; repository as its URL. Existing invocations and JSON export output remain unchanged when no selectors are provided; selector validation occurs before output so invalid requested selections always fail rather than silently producing empty columns. Add unit tests for repeatable flag parsing/exclusivity, name and ID resolution including errors, column order and empty values, all supported display types, and a mocked request assertion proving ID selection uses the fields already included in the item-list response.
operator.answer: OPERATOR_ANSWER: DESIGN_CHANGES_REQUIRED: Explicitly require selector flags to fail when combined with any explicit formatted or JSON output, field-definition pagination when selected columns are requested, and newline/carriage-return normalization. Also require deterministic ambiguity ordering and compact number formatting without forced trailing zeros.

operator.payload:
Add repeatable, mutually exclusive `--field <name>` and `--field-id <id>` flags to `gh project item-list`. Reject either selector flag when the invocation explicitly requests formatted/JSON output (`--format`, `--jq`, or `--template`) with a flag error, leaving existing JSON behavior unchanged.

For normal table output, fetch project items as today and use the field definitions embedded in that same response to resolve selectors. When selectors are present and the response reports further field-definition pages, fetch and append only the required continuation pages before resolution; do not perform a redundant initial field lookup. Thus projects with up to one page of fields make no extra field request, while any project can resolve a valid selected field beyond the first page.

Resolve each `--field` name case-insensitively and each `--field-id` exactly. Preserve selector order for appended table columns; headers use canonical resolved field names, normalized for line breaks. Unknown names report the supplied name and sorted available names; unknown IDs report sorted `name (id)` candidates; ambiguous names report matching IDs sorted lexically and direct users to `--field-id`. These validation errors occur before rendering, including if no items match. Existing behavior is unchanged when neither selector is supplied.

Append selected columns after Type, Title, Number, Repository, and ID. Render an empty cell where an item has no value. Convert all supplied field-value types into human-readable text: date/text/single-select directly; number using its shortest compact decimal representation without forced trailing zeros; iteration and milestone titles; labels, users, reviewers, and pull requests as comma-separated names or URLs; repository as its URL. Normalize CRLF, CR, and LF in headers and values to spaces so each logical item stays on one table row.

Add focused tests for repeatable parsing, exclusivity and output-mode rejection; case-insensitive name and exact-ID resolution with deterministic errors; selection order, normalized headers/cells, empty values, and every supported field-value display type; field pagination when requested; and mocked request counts proving no redundant field preflight occurs when the initial item response already contains all fields.
operator.answer: OPERATOR_ANSWER: DESIGN_CHANGES_REQUIRED: Include explicit rejection for all supported explicit JSON/format-output forms, retain a realistic repeated-selector help example, and require field values to be matched to selected columns by field node ID. Unknown field-value variants must render as empty cells.

operator.payload:
Add repeatable, mutually exclusive `--field <name>` and `--field-id <id>` flags to `gh project item-list`. Reject either selector flag with every explicit structured/format-output form supported by this command: `--format json`, `--jq`, and `--template` (including their valid combinations). The command has no `--json` flag. Add a realistic help example such as `gh project item-list 1 --owner monalisa --field Status --field Priority`.

For normal table output, fetch items as today and resolve selectors from the field definitions embedded in that response. If selectors are present and those definitions have additional pages, fetch and append only continuation pages before resolution; do not redundantly refetch the initial page. This provides complete field-definition resolution while avoiding an extra field-ID preflight whenever the initial response is sufficient.

Resolve names case-insensitively and IDs exactly. Unknown names report the supplied name plus sorted available names; unknown IDs report sorted `name (id)` candidates; ambiguous names report lexically sorted matching IDs and direct users to `--field-id`. All selector errors occur before rendering, even if no items match. Preserve selector order and append columns after Type, Title, Number, Repository, and ID; headers use canonical resolved names with CRLF, CR, and LF normalized to spaces.

For each selected column, match an item field value strictly by the selected field’s node ID, never by name or response position. Missing values and unknown field-value variants render empty cells. Render supported values as human-readable text: date/text/single-select directly; numbers in shortest compact decimal form with no forced trailing zeros; iteration and milestone titles; labels, users, reviewers, and pull requests as comma-separated names or URLs; repository as its URL. Normalize CRLF, CR, and LF in every rendered value to spaces.

Add tests for parsing, mutual exclusion, each explicit output-form rejection, the help example, deterministic selector failures, ID-based selected-value matching, selection order, normalization, empty and unknown values, all supported display types, field-definition pagination, and mocked request counts confirming no redundant first-page field preflight.
operator.answer: OPERATOR_ANSWER: DESIGN_CHANGES_REQUIRED: Specify that a field-definition continuation failure stops the command with a useful error before any table output. Also make multi-value rendering exact: labels use names, users use logins, reviewers use user logins and team names, and pull requests use URLs, each joined by comma and space.

findings.title: Required selected-field pagination failure and no-preflight behavior lack coverage
findings.evidence: `product.diff` lines 64-81 introduce the selected-field run path, but its tests only exercise `CompleteProjectFields` directly on one successful continuation (`product.diff` lines 496-547). There is no test that runs `item-list` with selectors and an initial item response, no continuation-failure/stdout assertion, and no mocked request-count assertion proving the initial fields page is not fetched again.
findings.why: The approved design explicitly requires no table output when a field continuation fails and mocked request counts proving no redundant first-page preflight. These are key user-visible correctness and efficiency guarantees of the new path; a direct helper success test cannot verify their command-level behavior.
findings.suggestedFix: Add command-level mocked tests for selector-enabled item listing: assert no second first-page fields request when the embedded fields page is sufficient; assert continuation pages are requested from the returned cursor; and make a continuation request fail, asserting a contextual error and empty table stdout.

reviewerResult.summary: The implementation appears to cover the core feature, but required end-to-end pagination/error and request-count behavior is not tested.
